topic: Earth's core is as hot as the Sun's surface
script: Earth's inner core is about as hot as the surface of the Sun. It is a ball of mostly iron and nickel at around 5,200 degrees Celsius. Even so, it is solid, because the pressure there is so enormous. Around it, an outer core of liquid metal swirls and flows. That moving metal creates Earth's magnetic field.
